body:
FOUND by a P5 honesty lens on T178 (2026-08-17), and it is the subtlest finding of the connector arc:
the overclaim is not in a FIELD, it is in the ACT of answering.

WHAT THE SPEC MAKES OF AN ANSWER. In the current MCP draft, `server/discover` is the ERA PROBE. The
versioning page states there is no negotiation handshake in the modern era: every request declares its
version in `_meta` (and the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header), and a server that cannot serve the
requested version MUST answer `-32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` listing what it supports. The
compatibility matrix says a dual-era client whose probe returns a `DiscoverResult` concludes the server
is MODERN and SHOULD CACHE THAT DECISION FOR THE LIFETIME OF THE ORIGIN.

WHAT THE DOOR ACTUALLY DOES. T178 answers `server/discover` honestly field by field — supportedVersions
is the real MCP_PROTOCOLS, capabilities and serverInfo are what `initialize` answers. But `_meta`
appears at exactly one site in src/server/http.ts: that response. There is no `-32022`, no
`MCP-Protocol-Version` handling, and no `protocolVersion` read outside `initialize`. So a client that
stays modern on the strength of the answer and then sends `tools/call` carrying a 2026-07-28 `_meta`
gets its call SERVED UNDER LEGACY SEMANTICS rather than refused — the matrix's own named failure,
"process an era-ambiguous method under legacy semantics".

WHY T178 SHIPPED ANYWAY, and this is the honest accounting rather than a defence: the mitigation is
real. `supportedVersions` lists only legacy revisions, so a compliant client reads the answer and
learns immediately that there is no mutual version. And the alternative — refusing `server/discover` —
is measured to break a live client outright (one Anthropic client treats the -32601 as a dead
connection and caches it). Answering imperfectly beats refusing, and the gap is named in the code
beside the discover case rather than left for a reader to discover.

THE WORK, in the order that keeps each step honest:
1. READ AND ENFORCE the requested version per request: the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header and the
   `_meta` protocol version, on every method rather than only `initialize`.
2. Answer `-32022` with the `supported` list when the requested version is not one this door speaks.
   Today an unspeakable version is silently served under whatever semantics the code happens to have.
3. DECIDE, and this is the real question the ticket exists to force: does Loam implement a modern
   revision, or does it stay legacy and answer discover only to say so? Both are defensible. What is
   not defensible is the current middle, where the answer implies an era the door does not keep.
4. If a modern revision is adopted, `MCP_PROTOCOLS` gains it only WITH its semantics — the T178 rails
   deliberately cannot prove a version is implemented, only that it is announced, and the comment
   there says so.

RAILS: a request carrying a version the door does not speak is refused with -32022 and the refusal
lists the supported set; a request carrying a version it DOES speak is served; and the two-sided one
that matters — a modern-era client's `tools/call` is either served under modern semantics or refused,
never served under legacy semantics while the client believes otherwise.

TIER: Myk's, because step 3 decides what the store promises about a protocol era.
title: Answering server/discover declares the door MODERN, and the door enforces no per-request version
